I love SWAT 4, this game has been called the spiritual successor to the SWAT series many times, but I'm not too sure it is. The aesthetics, the strory, the situations, and environments simply aren't aligned with the simple, "another day at the office" nature of SWAT 4. That said, it's not a bad game, but if you're just craving SWAT 4, load up Rainbow Six 3, or start another SEF career. 
Drama, twisted words, unfulfilled promises, censorship aside, The game is good. If you love slower, tactical shooters, and the idea of leveraging your small team's equipment and planning to defeat a larger force that is more than capable of folding you like a lawn chair in a fair fight, then you'll like Ready Or Not.

I've been following Ready Or Not (RON)'s development since it was originally announced in 2017. I've been excited for a new SWAT game, terribly disappointed by the PvP alpha, and delightfully surprised with a half-decent release, and a solid (albeit bumpy) development through early access. The core of the game is good. Suspects are accurate, varied, deadly, and interesting. Your own AI sometimes leaves you wondering if the nursing home is having a field day at the police department, but is usually helpful in a way that feels quite decent - They don't require much baby-sitting and can be trusted to execute a well thought-out breach.

The maps/environment are one of the games biggest strengths, though not perfect. They're interesting and varied, and almost always have their own story to tell through the environment and suspects. They're designed in a way that poses a real challenge in how to best approach certain positions. The stories they tell are really neat and it's fun to piece together what's been going on. They are HUGE though, absolutely massive. They span huge distances, multiple floors, have tens of suspects, and it all leads to an extra gameplay consideration that I'm not very fond of: Attrition. The main challenge of the game is no longer about outsmarting the AI, saving hostages, etc. It becomes all about managing equipment expenditure, damage taken to yourself and you squad, and simply surviving each encounter through a job the national guard left the LSPD on hold for. 
I feel like this is one of the main considerations that the game is balanced around as well. On most missions, you're left clearing out the last few rooms with little or no equipment, a few gunshot wounds, maybe a dead teammate, and one last suspect. It's fun, but it's something that feels very out of place in a SWAT/police game. After you've solved the Waco siege with yourself and 4 men, you'll be left scouring the floor for any weapons or civilians you've missed. 

That is my main critique of the game. The vast majority of these scenarios your single swat team is called in to handle are jobs for the national guard, or at the very least far more than one lone SWAT team squad. Though there are some more reasonable missions throughout the game, such as the "Thank you, Come again"/gas station mission. It's comparable to SWAT 4's take on a convenience store robbery gone wrong, but RON's is far larger. 

There is some controversy regarding the censorship of certain parts of the game. Dismemberment of incapacitated suspects, nudity, a child overdosed and dying, etc. It's all inconsequential imo, but I understand the frustration around it. Mods to reverse these changes have been removed many times as well. Research it and vote with your money if you really care. My complaint regarding censorship is from a different change made before what was mentioned above. The mission "Elephant" has you responding to an active shooter at a college campus. The fact that the mission takes place in a college, full of adults, rather than a K-12 school as indicated by trailers and other pre-release material feels like a cop-out. I recall that idea of including a level involving a school shooting being a not insignifcant selling-point from VOID regarding the "no holds barred," "reality of police/SWAT," etc, nature of the game. The idea that the brutal reality of a SWAT team's work to be displayed by the game was present. As the game grew, got more popular, topped steam charts, had prospects of console releases, etc, there existed a pressure to sanitize and trim the unsightly elements used to advertise the game in the first place. I think the recent censorship controversies are an extension of that universalization that certain store fronts and advertisers demand.

That said, the game *is* great. There's a pretty good amount of replayability, the guns are cool (i miss the carry handle M4), there's mods (no workshop tho), the stories the environments tell are fun to discover, it's great with friends, and for what you get, I'd say the price is reasonable. Research the controversies yourself and vote with your money as you see fit.

A good game, or at least I thought so for a while. In terms of realism, the game is incredibly accurate and awesome. The experience is similar to when you were a kid watching SWAT shows and imagining yourself being part of them. If you play with friends, the game is absolutely worth it, and I highly recommend it. That's not the reason for my negative review, though. As a solo player like me, who mainly plays singleplayer games like this, I simply cannot recommend it because the bot AI is absolutely terrible. Take the "Clear" command, for example. I've had so many situations where the bots couldn't even clear an entire room because someone was still hiding inside, they got stuck on something, or they opened another door and got shot to pieces by an enemy while just standing there. The same thing happened several times with "Fall In." The bots couldn't defend themselves, and I always had to take out the enemies myself. Of course, you can't complete the mission properly because you keep getting shot and eventually die. Without the bots, playing solo is extremely difficult, so I simply cannot recommend this game to solo players. And judging by other reviews, I'm not the only one who has noticed these issues.

Well, when it comes to tactical gunplay and realism, this is probably as good as it gets for now. The only other game that comes to mind is Bodycam, but that is more of an online shooter. Ready or Not is insanely immersive. You genuinely feel like you can die easily if you walk into a room like an idiot. The game is certainly not easy, especially on higher difficulties. You have to take it seriously, prep your gear, and make sure you bring a variety of resources for breaching and ambushing.

Everything you could desire in an arsenal is here. There is an insane amount of guns in each category, including shotguns, SMGs, and assault rifles. Assault rifles definitely feel like the meta because they combine great firepower and excellent control. The German G36C rifle feels like the absolute best option, but some people prefer others. You also get different pistols, attachments, and tons of gear choices. You can even choose to play with a six-shooter if you want. Unlocking cosmetic rewards also feels very good. It lets you fully customize your character so you do not have to play as a blank slate.

It is also really cool that your AI crew has actual identities. Your people can die, and if they do, they are gone forever. They can also get too stressed out and you have to send them to therapy, meaning you cannot just use the same team all the time. It is a bit of a nuisance sometimes, but it feels highly realistic. It is rewarding because they can unlock modifiers that give you bonuses, and you can see their names and backgrounds.

However, the game's performance is not very good. In my opinion, it is not very well optimized. The gameplay can feel a bit janky, wanky, and clanky at times. It does not always run smoothly. The controls can also be difficult, especially when trying to give commands to your crew. It is sometimes hard to get the AI to do exactly what you want because the command system is not very smooth.
Overall, it still feels very nice. If you want to play as a SWAT unit, this is the definitive game to go to. No other title on the market is going to give you a better swatting experience than this one.
